lineage: Round-robin arbitration: when several requesters compete for one shared resource, grant fairly in rotation so none starves; the arbiter is a small finite-state DECISION machine at the heart of buses, NoCs and schedulers
version: github.com/freecores/round_robin_arbiter master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)
build_system: iverilog + a Techne testbench driving request vectors
entry_points: the arbiter module: request[] in, grant[] out, with a rotating priority pointer

example.command: Techne testbench: assert several request lines at once across cycles, capture which gets the grant each cycle
example.output: the grant sequence -- fair rotation, no starvation

upstream_docs: Dally & Towles, Principles and Practices of Interconnection Networks

human_capability_summary.built_to: decide, each clock, which of several simultaneous requesters gets a shared resource, rotating priority so every requester is served and none is starved
human_capability_summary.pressure: more requesters than resources, arriving simultaneously; a fixed-priority scheme starves low-priority requesters under load
human_capability_summary.success_means: every requester eventually granted (no starvation), with bounded waiting, at one grant per cycle

known_human_problem_solved: fair arbitration of a shared hardware resource
human_environmental_pressure: resource contention: simultaneous competing requests for one grant
human_failure_condition: starvation: a requester never gets the resource; or a grant collision (two grants at once) corrupts the shared bus
behavioral_entry_point: drive all request lines high every cycle and confirm the grant rotates; hold one requester high forever and confirm others still progress

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run verilog-rr-arbiter
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: decide, each clock, which of several simultaneous requesters gets a shared resource, rotating priority so every requester is served and none is starved
